According to the latest report from Counterpoint Research, despite the overall industry slump, Apple's iPhone shipments still grew 3% year-over-year, setting a historic high of 20% share of global smartphone shipments. Details are as follows.

Second lowest level for a second quarter since 2013

Counterpoint Research stated that in the second quarter of 2026, Samsung led the global smartphone market with a 24% shipment share, followed closely by Apple with 20% (a historic high for the quarter), Xiaomi with 12%, OPPO with 11%, and vivo with 8%.

Compared with the same period last year, Samsung's market share rose by four percentage points, Apple rose by three percentage points, vivo rose by one percentage point, Xiaomi fell by two percentage points, OPPO fell by one percentage point. The combined share of other manufacturers dropped from 28% to 26%.

Counterpoint pointed out that Samsung regained the top spot in global smartphone shipments in the second quarter of 2026, after Apple had led in the first quarter on the back of strong iPhone 17 demand.

During the second quarter of 2026, Apple was the only major OEM that did not raise prices; Samsung, on the other hand, benefited from strong demand for the Galaxy S26 series, improved product supply, and more aggressive promotional campaigns, growing at a faster pace.

Looking ahead, Counterpoint expects that "global smartphone shipments for the full year will decline by about 14%, and the global memory shortage is expected to persist until 2027." The firm noted that until supply conditions improve, manufacturers will continue to cut low-margin models, adjust storage configurations, and rely more on refurbished units and previous-generation products.
